PyTorch, with kokoro ```bash pip install "inno-kokoro[torch]" ``` ```python from inno_kokoro.enroll import Tuner, enroll, read import torch from kokoro import KPipeline tuner = Tuner(backend="torch") # caches model from HF on first use pack, _ = enroll(*read("my_ref.wav"), tuner, return_pt=True) # [510, 1, 256] torch.save(pack, "am_me.pt") pipe = KPipeline(lang_code="a") wav = next(pipe("Hello from a tuned voice.", voice=pack)).audio ```
ONNX (no torch), with kokoro-onnx ```bash pip install inno-kokoro kokoro-onnx ``` ```python from inno_kokoro.enroll import Tuner, enroll, read import numpy as np from kokoro_onnx import Kokoro tuner = Tuner(backend="onnx") # downloads model.safetensors + model.onnx on first use pack, _ = enroll(*read("my_ref.wav"), tuner) # [510, 1, 256] float32 NumPy np.save("am_me.npy", pack) kokoro = Kokoro("kokoro-v1.0.onnx", "voices-v1.0.bin") # from the kokoro-onnx releases wav, sr = kokoro.create("Hello from a tuned voice.", voice=pack, lang="en-us") ```
Notes: - prefix names with stock accent+gender codes for use in other libraries: e.g `af_`, `am_`, `bf_`, `bm_` - pitch ceiling is set automatically - `enroll(..., fmax=180)`: can override when needed (archival sources, etc) ### ONNX `model.onnx`: the speaker encoder and style head for onnxruntime (fp32, 31.5 MB). Used by `Tuner(backend="onnx")` from inno-kokoro 0.4.0. Same packs as torch, about 2x faster on CPU.
Graph details - input `fbank` [1, frames, 80] float32: kaldi log-mel of the first 30 s at 16 kHz (`inno_kokoro/fbank.py`) - outputs `embedding` [1, 512] (unit, UniSpeech-SAT-sv space) and `style` [1, 256] - opset 20, standard ops only, no DFT or custom ops - matches torch within 5.4e-7 on 540 clips ([parity check](onnx_parity.md)) - exported with `export_onnx.py` (inno-kokoro `tools/export_onnx.py` at b442727) | reference | onnxruntime | torch | |---|---|---| | 8 s | 100 ms | 165 ms | | 30 s | 410 ms | 890 ms | CPU (best of 5 runs)
### Architecture A 5 to 30 s reference clip in, a stock-shaped Kokoro voice pack out. Everything loads from `model.safetensors`, no extra downloads.
Architecture details Enrollment embeds an input audio sample via the baked speaker encoder and maps through `model.safetensors` to build the encoder side; prosody aspects are measured to build the predictor half. - **speaker encoder**: a 6.6M-param WeSpeaker ResNet34 distilled from [**UniSpeech-SAT-sv**](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/unispeech-sat-base-plus-sv) embeddings - matches within 0.002 speaker cosine on hold-out dev-clean (380mb fp32 -> 14mb fp16) - **style head**: the decoder (timbre) half of the pack comes from the speaker embedding (512) mapped to Kokoro style (256). Shifts along a learned spectral-tilt direction by the reference's measured tilt. - **prosody blend**: the predictor (prosody) half uses the stock Kokoro packs as a foundation: - Blended by nonnegative least squares to the reference F0 mean, F0 spread and syllable rate. - Packs more than 4 st from the reference's pitch are excluded. - Higher graded packs are weighted as preferred during selection. - **prosody head** (v0.2): a linear adjust on the blend from the reference's F0 mean and spread, - fitted to deltas optimized through the frozen predictor. `enroll(..., head=False)` skips it. Enrollment runs in about 0.05 s per second of reference on CPU (a 30 s reference in 1.4 s) and 0.1-0.3 s total on a GPU, after the one-time model load. Total model size @ fp16: ~24mb
## Limits - English trained (LibriTTS-R) currently - Some texture/identity is traded to maintain audio quality and stability within Kokoro's range. - Rythym is a best-effort match to the speaker. - Prosody is a convex blend of stock prosody by pitch, spread and pace. Outside of that range, it will only pin to the nearest edge - Reference clip requirements: - 3 second minimum, up to a max of 30s - Reasonably free of audio artifacts - Single speaker ## Training and Metrics All stages: Kokoro frozen; LibriTTS-R train-clean-100 unless noted. Trained via HF Jobs `a10g-small`; under $20 in GPU time:
v0.1.0 training notes - Stage 1: mapped speaker embedding to timbre: - Style head on a speaker-embedding cycle loss: clone, render, re-embed, cosine to the input audio embedding. - [10k steps: dev cosine ~0.92; nearest stock voice baseline 0.857] - Stage 2: the embedding alone missed texture and pitch; adjustments: - Augmented pitch and speed. Added losses via a WavLM layer-statistics L1, a small log-F0 error, and spectral-tilt. - [11k steps: dev cosine 0.934, DNSMOS 3.30] - Stage 3: tuned the encoder side to match the blended predictors: - Predictor half fixed to the blended rows, only the decoder half trained. - [3k steps: dev cosine 0.932, DNSMOS 3.48] - Stage 4: distilled the speaker encoder so enrollment needs no UniSpeech download: - WeSpeaker ResNet34 plus a projection, trained on `1 - cos(student, teacher)` over LibriTTS-R crops with synthetic channel damage; the style head is untouched. - [20k steps: hold-out dev-clean parity, DNSMOS equal; archival references sat about 0.05 behind the teacher] - Stage 5: the student lagged the teacher on archival references; synthetic damage had plateaued: - Mixed real public-domain archival broadcast audio into the distillation crops. - [8k steps: archival cosine up 0.03-0.05, DNSMOS unchanged]
v0.2.0 training notes - Stage 1: the blend under-predicted pitch range and sentence-final falls: - Fitted a predictor-half delta per speaker (426; adds VoxPopuli-en and Emilia-YODAS EN) - Targeted F0 mean, spread, IQR, pause fraction and speech time. - Ridge head from reference F0 mean + spread to the fitted delta. - [hold-out: F0 mean error 0.9 -> 0.45 st, spread 0.6 -> 0.35 st, IQR 0.9 -> 0.5 st] - Stage 2: the student trailed the teacher on public-speaking and in-the-wild references: - Added VoxPopuli and Emilia speakers to the distillation crops. - [8k steps: hold-out cosine VoxPopuli 0.976 -> 0.986, Emilia 0.964 -> 0.983; WavLM cosine 0.941 -> 0.944, DNSMOS unchanged] - Stage 3: the timbre half had only seen LibriTTS speakers: - Repeated v0.1.0 stage 3 with VoxPopuli and Emilia speakers in the draw. - [3k steps: WavLM cosine samples 0.927 -> 0.935, dev-clean 0.956 -> 0.959, VoxPopuli 0.926 -> 0.939, Emilia 0.931 -> 0.936; DNSMOS unchanged]
### Zero-shot identity benchmark Inno gets about a third of the normalized similarity range, twice as close as the nearest stock pack (with UTMOS intact and keeping Kokoro's stable natural style).
Full benchmark results and methodology LibriSpeech test-clean, F5-TTS cross-sentence split (1127 utterances, 39 held-out speakers. Reference in, new sentence out, scored against the speaker's real recording. - normalized: how far the render sits between sounding like a stranger (0) and a second real take of the speaker (1) - RTF: RTX 4060 Ti | system | SIM-o | normalized | ECAPA | UTMOS | RTF | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | ground truth (second recording) | 0.695 | 1.00 | 0.656 | 4.10 | | | F5-TTS v1 base | 0.650 | 0.94 | 0.713 | 3.86 | 0.48 | | StyleTTS2 (LibriTTS zero-shot) | 0.386 | 0.46 | 0.415 | 4.40 | 0.06 | | **Inno v0.2** | 0.288 | 0.32 | 0.288 | 4.45 | 0.07 | | OpenVoice v2 | 0.227 | 0.23 | 0.316 | 3.80 | 0.12 | | Kokoro, nearest stock pack | 0.167 | 0.15 | 0.215 | 4.25 | 0.06 | StyleTTS2 uses a related architecture with an unfrozen decoder, a possible ceiling for this style space. - StyleTTS2: alpha 0.3, beta 0.7, 5 steps. - OpenVoice v2: MeloTTS EN-US, tau 0.3. - F5-TTS: 32 NFE, CFG 2.
v0.1 vs v0.2 shipped-weight comparison Measured on the shipped weights through the stock `KPipeline`: one fixed passage rendered for the seven sample voices plus ten hold-out dev-clean speakers, F0 by Praat over 6 s chunks with the reference's tracking ceiling applied to both sides. | metric | v0.1 blend only | v0.2 with head | |---|---|---| | speaker cosine (WavLM-sv), samples / dev-clean | 0.926 / 0.956 | 0.935 / 0.959 | | F0 mean, render minus reference | 0.65 st mean abs | 0.8 st mean abs | | F0 spread, render minus reference | 0.65 st mean abs | 0.5 st mean abs | | DNSMOS | 3.50 | 3.50 | The head's gain is spread; on F0 mean it scatters more per speaker and flips the signed bias from -0.2 to +0.3 st.
## Licenses and credits Adapter weights and code: Apache-2.0, except the baked speaker encoder (`enc.*` in `model.safetensors`), which is CC BY-SA 3.0 (see below) - Built on [hexgrad/Kokoro-82M](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) (Apache-2.0, StyleTTS2 architecture) - The speaker encoder is a [WeSpeaker](https://github.com/wenet-e2e/wespeaker) ResNet34 (code Apache-2.0) - initialised from the [VoxCeleb-trained ResNet34-LM weights](https://huggingface.co/Wespeaker/wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM) (CC BY 4.0) - distilled from [microsoft/unispeech-sat-base-plus-sv](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/unispeech-sat-base-plus-sv) - (Microsoft UniSpeech, [CC BY-SA 3.0 on GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/UniSpeech/blob/main/LICENSE)); encoder weights under CC BY-SA 3.0 - Training data (no audio redistributed beyond the samples): - [LibriTTS-R](https://www.openslr.org/141/) (CC BY 4.0), also the LibriTTS sample references - [VoxPopuli](https://github.com/facebookresearch/voxpopuli) (CC0) - [Emilia-YODAS](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amphion/Emilia-Dataset) EN (CC BY 4.0) - Sample references: - Amelia Earhart from ["Speech by Amelia Earhart"](https://www.loc.gov/item/afccal000004/), Library of Congress AFC 1986/022 - Jane Goodall from [BBC Woman's Hour excerpt](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jane_Goodall_BBC_Radio4_Woman%27s_Hour_26_Jan_2010_p00tr6ks.flac), BBC, CC BY 3.0 - Vincent Price public domain from ["The House On Haunted Hill"](https://archive.org/details/The_House_On_Haunted_Hill) Only clone voices you have permission to clone, even the shallow cloning offered via this model and technique.

# PhoWhisper-Qwen ASR

Mô hình nhận dạng giọng nói tiếng Việt kết hợp **PhoWhisper** và **Qwen LLM**:
- **Audio Encoder**: `vinai/PhoWhisper-medium`
- **LLM Decoder**: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`
- **Adapter**: Conv1D (4x Downsampling) + MLP Projector
- **Nguồn trọng số Checkpoint**: `namkiett/phowhisper-qwen-phoaudio/phoaudio_final.pt`

## 🚀 Hướng dẫn sử dụng nhanh (Quickstart)

Cài đặt thư viện:
```bash
pip install -q transformers accelerate safetensors librosa soundfile torch
```

Chỉ cần 3 dòng code để gọi AutoModel:
```python
from transformers import AutoModel

# 1. Nạp mô hình trực tiếp từ Hugging Face Hub
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    "namkiett/phowhisper-qwen-asr",
    trust_remote_code=True
).to("cuda")

# 2. Nhận diện giọng nói từ file âm thanh (.wav, .mp3, ...) hoặc numpy array 16kHz
text = model.transcribe("duong_dan_file_am_thanh.wav")
print("Văn bản nhận diện:", text)
```

# Eka (एक) · audio8-nepali

Eka is Ampixa's Nepali fine-tune of [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b).
Give it a few seconds of someone speaking and some Nepali text, and it reads the text in that voice.
The release checkpoint is **eka-ft-v7**. Release page: [ampixa.com/eka](https://ampixa.com/eka/).

## Try it on a CPU in two minutes

No GPU, no PyTorch, no account needed. `onnx/` is eka-ft-v7 and `onnx-v9/` is eka-ft-v9, both ONNX INT8 for CPUs.

```bash
pip install "onnxruntime==1.23.2" "numpy<2.5" soundfile scipy tokenizers huggingface_hub
hf download ampixa/audio8-nepali --include "onnx/*" --include "onnx-v9/*" --include "runtime/*" \
    --include "voices/*" --include "examples/*" --local-dir eka      # about 1.6 GB (each model alone: about 820 MB)
cd eka

# Built-in voice (OpenSLR 43 speaker 0546)
python examples/speak.py --text "नमस्ते, म एक हुँ। म नेपाली बोल्छु।" --out hello.wav               # eka-ft-v7
python examples/speak.py --model v9 --text "नमस्ते, म एक हुँ। म नेपाली बोल्छु।" --out hello_v9.wav  # eka-ft-v9

# Your own voice: 4 to 10 seconds of one person speaking, and exactly what they say in it
python examples/speak.py --model v9 --ref me.wav --ref-text "मेरो नाम राम हो, म काठमाडौँमा बस्छु।" \
                         --text "आज बेलुका खाना खान घर आउँछु।" --out me.wav
```

Want only one model? Download `onnx/*` for v7 or `onnx-v9/*` for v9 (about 820 MB each; the codec files are the same).
Each `--include` takes one pattern.

It prints how long the audio is and how long it took. On an Apple M3 Pro with 4 threads we measured RTF 1.18 on a
39-second paragraph (a little slower than real time); short sentences take longer per second of audio because the
voice prompt is processed first. v7 and v9 run at the same speed. If a sentence comes out empty or runs on, try another `--seed`.

**Known problem:** on an Intel i5-10400 (AVX2, no VNNI) the INT8 build produced broken audio for most test sentences,
while the same files and settings were fine on Apple Silicon. Test on your own CPU before relying on it on older Intel
machines; we are working on a fix.

## v7 or v9?

Both run the same way; pick with `--model`.

- **eka-ft-v9: fewer word and pronunciation errors.** Choose it when the words matter most: reading text aloud,
  announcements, anything where a wrong word is worse than a slightly different voice.
- **eka-ft-v7: closer voice match.** Choose it when sounding like the reference speaker matters most. It is the
  checkpoint the release film and benchmarks headline.

If unsure, render the same sentence with both and listen. On 20 public NepTTS-Bench sentences with the built-in voice
and the same seed, the CPU builds scored 12.5% (v7) and 10.2% (v9) character error by the MMS recognizer; v9 was better
on 10 sentences, worse on 6, tied on 4.

## Which checkpoint to use

All nine fine-tunes are here under release names. The root `model.safetensors` is eka-ft-v7.

| Release | File | What it is | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| eka-ft-v1 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v1/` | Wave 1 supervised (318.8 h), step 6000 | `327bca23…` |
| eka-ft-v2 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v2/` | Wave 2 supervised (575 h), step 3000 | `dcaa61f9…` |
| eka-ft-v3 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v3/` | Wave 2 supervised, step 6000 | `4452b7c8…` |
| eka-ft-v4 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v4/` | Wave 3 supervised, final | `73e1c134…` |
| eka-ft-v5 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v5/` | Wave 4 supervised, step 2000 | `30512a90…` |
| eka-ft-v6 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v6/` | Preference training (DPO), round 1 | `eb0f19e5…` |
| **eka-ft-v7** | `model.safetensors`, `checkpoints/eka-ft-v7/`, `onnx/` | **DPO round 2. The release.** | `a555f6c0…` |
| eka-ft-v8 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v8/` | DPO round 3, step 129 | `0ab717ef…` |
| eka-ft-v9 | `checkpoints/eka-ft-v9/`, `onnx-v9/` | DPO round 3, step 258. Fewest word errors | `451ef4a9…` |

- **On a CPU:** eka-ft-v7 (`onnx/`) and eka-ft-v9 (`onnx-v9/`).
- **Most accurate words:** eka-ft-v9, on every independent recognizer we used, at a small cost in voice match.
- The others are PyTorch only (load them with this repo's `modeling_arktts.py`; a GPU is recommended).

| | eka-ft-v7 | eka-ft-v8 | eka-ft-v9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Character error, 23 voices not in training (MMS) | 16.3% | 15.1% | **12.6%** |
| Character error, Naamche cloning bench clean | 8.8% | 8.7% | **7.5%** |
| Voice match, Naamche cloning bench (ECAPA) | **0.52** | 0.51 | 0.48 |
| Hindi Leak Scorer flags | 18 / 103 | not run | **15 / 103** |

No significance test has been run between these three. The Zipformer-55k recognizer was part of the v8/v9 training
reward, so its scores are not used here.

## How it compares

Naamche cloning bench v1.1, clean track, 64 prompt and sentence pairs (our harness reproduces Swar's published numbers):

| System | Character error | Voice match | UTMOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Eka (eka-ft-v7)** | 8.8% | 0.52 | 3.24 |
| Swar | 5.6% | 0.69 | 2.67 |
| OmniVoice | 5.0% | 0.70 | 2.63 |
| VoxCPM2 | 9.0% | 0.68 | 2.40 |
| Audio8 base | 84.5% | 0.34 | 2.73 |

[Hindi Leak Scorer](https://ampixa.com/blog/does-a-nepali-tts-voice-still-say-it-the-hindi-way/) v84 (frozen), same
26 sentences in 4 voices: IndicF5 60/93, VoxCPM2 55/91, Swar 36/100, OmniVoice 34/104, **Eka v7 18/103**, Eka v9 15/103.
A flag is a candidate for a listener, not a confirmed error.

Generator size: Eka 170M parameters (plus a 130M codec decoder), Swar 337M, OmniVoice 613M, VoxCPM2 2.31B.

All of these are automatic scores; there is no listening panel yet. Training exposure of the bench voices is unknown
for every system, so the tables are not rankings. Eka's weakest point is voice match.

## Files

- `model.safetensors`, `config.json`, `modeling_arktts*.py`, `processing_arktts.py`, tokenizer files, `codec.pth`:
  the PyTorch model (root weights = eka-ft-v7; until 2026-11-11 the root was eka-ft-v1).
- `checkpoints/eka-ft-v1` … `eka-ft-v9`: every fine-tune, by release name.
- `onnx/`: eka-ft-v7 ONNX INT8 (same files as [ampixa/audio8-nepali-dpo-onnx](https://huggingface.co/ampixa/audio8-nepali-dpo-onnx)
  @75800398). `onnx/registration/` is the codec encoder used to register new voices.
- `onnx-v9/`: eka-ft-v9 ONNX INT8, made with the same weight-swap method onto Audio8's INT8 graphs
  ([Edge0/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/audio8-TTS-0.1B-ONNX-INT8)); that method reproduces the
  `onnx/` v7 build byte for byte. Codec, encoder and tokenizer files are identical to `onnx/`.
- `runtime/arktts_runtime_0_1b/`: the ONNX runtime from [Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS](https://github.com/Audio8-AI/Audio8_TTS)
  @4eb54a69, unmodified, Apache-2.0.
- `voices/slr43-0546/`: a sample voice from OpenSLR 43 (Google, ne_np_female), CC BY-SA 4.0.
- `examples/speak.py`: the test script above.

## Licence and use

Weights: [Audio8 Community License v1.0](https://huggingface.co/Audio8/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.1b). It bars commercial use at
or above US$2M annual revenue and requires consent before cloning a real person's voice. Clone only voices you have
permission to use, and disclose synthetic speech where required. The runtime is Apache-2.0; the sample voice is
CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution: OpenSLR 43, Google).

# Gronings OmniVoice

A Gronings (Groningen Low Saxon, `gos`) LoRA adapter for
[k2-fsa/OmniVoice](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice), trained by
[Wietse de Vries (@wietsedv)](https://huggingface.co/wietsedv).

This E2-4000 release was trained on GroTTS (~12 hours, 3 narrators) and validated
proaten speech (~13 hours, 797 speakers). It generates 24 kHz audio.

**Try it:** [Gronings TTS Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/VanModers114/Gronings-TTS).
Provide 3–10 seconds of clean reference speech and its exact transcript to choose
the speaker.

**Local inference:** download
[VanModers114/gronings-omnivoice](https://huggingface.co/VanModers114/gronings-omnivoice)
and use the included `model.py` loader and `textnorm.py` normalizer with OmniVoice.
The adapter requires the base model and audio codec, downloaded on first use.
Use language `gos`, `num_step=64`, and `guidance_scale=1.5`.

Automatic CER is 4.0% on held-out GroTTS sentences and 4.8% on unseen proaten
speakers.
